design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller asks one thing - what will you pay on my hospital claim from Porto - and the answer is
6658.00, a figure that depends on three things he never mentions and one field that flatly
contradicts it. The policy record says his high deductible is met (deductible_accumulated 2910.00
against a 2870.00 deductible), so the lazy answer is 7896.00. In fact three of the paid lines that
built that accumulator fall on days before the policy took effect: the supplement settled them in
error, one of them paid the caller himself. The representative must read the policy's own rule, see
that the settlement waits on the money he was paid being sent back, work back to the restatement
that waits behind it, book the restatement, hand the repayment to the caller, and only then settle
the waiting line - and at every step the figure rests on a different part of the claim record.

SCOPE: ALREADY OCCUPIED / CLAIMED HERE / RESERVED
Task 0 occupied the premium side: medigap_ext_dual_coverage_premium_return and
medigap_ext_premium_account_settlement, on the base policies medigap_premium_rating and
medigap_premium_billing_and_posting, with the tools post_overlap_premium_return_c83152d2 and
remit_supplement_settlement_23b5df61. This task claims the claims side and nothing else:
medigap_ext_uncovered_day_line_restatement and medigap_ext_uncovered_day_direct_repayment (subject
medigap_claim_adjustment, on medigap_claim_adjustment_and_recovery) and
medigap_ext_crossover_benefit_settlement (subject medigap_claim_crossover_processed, on
medigap_benefit_payment), with the tools book_precoverage_restatement_aba9484f,
repay_direct_benefit_f162ba18 and settle_crossover_benefit_9f3dc765. No policy, tool, base subject
event or computed quantity is shared with task 0, and with these five policies the difficulty's
extended charter is complete.

THE DRAW (Step 0, scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/tasks/medicare_supplement_policy_desk --task 1)
{"task": 1, "key": "env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/1",
 "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 4]}
The tree therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems and three computations carrying six, five
and four factors. The restatement takes the six, the settlement (the root) takes the five and the
repayment takes the four.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root problem: medigap_ext_crossover_benefit_settlement - the figure the caller rang about.
Chain: settlement <- repayment <- restatement. Topological order: restatement, repayment,
settlement.
Edge 1: settlement <- repayment, kind value_input, gate counted_toward_deductible (a compute binding
of the settlement), form state.
  Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the settlement's own rule: "What the supplement pays on a
  line waiting on it is fixed only after the claim record carries the entry recording the money the
  policyholder has sent back on the lines the supplement paid her for days the policy did not
  cover."
  Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result -
  what the supplement pays on the line it settles - to what it waits on, in the affirmative
  direction; the negated rewriting ("is not fixed until the claim record carries ...") states the
  same dependency with nothing added, dropped or split. The affirmative direction is the one a
  benefit desk uses for a payment it will make once the file is square, which is how the desk that
  settles a claim would put it. (2) The side it waits on is a record-visible state - an entry on the
  claim record recording money recovered from the policyholder - named in the words the claim record
  and its finder use. (3) No tool, policy id, snake_case token or row id. (4) Its strength is the
  edge's: a hard "only after", scoped to the lines the supplement paid her for days the policy did
  not cover, no wider and no narrower than the condition.
  State-form legality: exactly one write of this difficulty brings an entry of that kind about,
  repay_direct_benefit_f162ba18, the target tool of the repayment policy; the restatement tool books
  an entry of the adjusted kind, not a recovery from the policyholder.
  Derivation: the sentence says the settlement waits on a recovery entry. The claim record
  (find_medigap_claim_crossovers) shows one entry of the adjustment family, the restatement of 15
  July 2026 against the February line, carrying the status adjusted - not a recovery from the
  policyholder - so the state does not hold. Reading the repayment policy's own rule, which says
  what such an entry records and that its result is what the policyholder sends back, its target
  tool is the one write that brings the state about, and it must come first.
Edge 2: repayment <- restatement, kind value_input, gate recovered_from_others (a compute binding of
the repayment), form state.
  Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the repayment's own rule: "What the policyholder is asked to
  send back is fixed only after the claim record carries the entry taking back what the supplement
  paid on the lines that fall outside cover and reached someone other than her."
  Four-point test: (1) "only after" joins this policy's own result - what the policyholder is asked
  to send back - to the state it waits on, affirmatively; the negated rewriting is exact. A recovery
  unit states it this way because it will not ask a member for money until it has taken back what it
  can from the provider. (2) A record-visible state: an entry on the claim record taking back what
  was paid to someone other than her. (3) No tool, id or code token. (4) Exactly the scope of the
  condition: the lines outside cover that reached someone else.
  State-form legality: only book_precoverage_restatement_aba9484f books an entry taking back money
  paid to someone other than the policyholder; the repayment tool's own entries record money
  recovered from her.
  Derivation: the record shows such an entry for the February line only, so the state does not hold
  for the January line whose 134.00 went to the provider; the restatement policy's rule says its
  result is the liability such an entry restates, so its write is the one that brings the state
  about.
  Seed evidence that each edge is false at the opening is recorded in prerequisite_closure, down to
  the row and field.
  The customer's own write: the repayment is his - repay_direct_benefit_f162ba18 is owner=user,
  unlocked and handed to him at that problem's place in the order. In-person semantics: it is his
  own money going back, he says so ("the only thing you will not have done for you is money leaving
  your own bank"), and it completes on the spot.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Write subject medigap_claim_adjustment (the restatement and the repayment). Governing base policy:
medigap_claim_adjustment_and_recovery.
  original_line_on_record: "The adjustment names the single processed crossover line it applies to,
  and that line is on record with a claim status of paid or adjusted." Evidence: the source line's
  own row, claim_status paid, correlated to the write through source_claim_id. Both writes name one
  line and one line only - the rule that a Medicare claim covering several services is never
  adjusted as one is why the two lines of claim K26012045871 are restated separately, one by the
  plan and one by the policyholder.
  adjustment_not_already_posted: "No adjustment of that same processed crossover line is already on
  record." The only adjustment standing at the opening names the February line, so neither of this
  task's two source lines carries one.
Write subject medigap_claim_crossover_processed (the settlement). Governing base policy:
medigap_benefit_payment.
  policy_in_force_on_service_date: the policy stands active and took effect 2026-03-01, and the line
  settled has a date of service of 2026-06-18, inside cover. The same gate is what the two problems
  before it are about: the lines of 20 January and 4 February are outside it, which is why the
  supplement should never have settled them.
  medicare_determination_on_record: Medicare determined the foreign claim and 9400.00 stands
  recorded as approved on the line; the other waiting line carries no approved amount at all, so
  Medicare has not determined it and it is not settled. No base eligibility on any of the three
  writes is a time gate, so temporal_feasibility is empty.
Declared override: the settlement replaces base's calendar-year sentence for the high deductible
with a rolling twelve months to date, declared clause by clause in overwrite. Everything else of
medigap_benefit_payment is inherited untouched - the share worked out from the amount Medicare
approved, the excess charges arising only where the provider does not accept assignment, the
foreign travel deductible, coinsurance and lifetime maximum.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Target of the restatement: the first line of Medicare claim K26012045871, dated 2026-01-20, which
crossed over automatically and on which the supplement paid the provider 134.00. Correlation key:
source_claim_id. Rows entering its arithmetic: that line and the February line (the liability
outside cover), the standing restatement against the February line (what has already been taken
back), and the member's Advantage enrollment (what is left with him).
Target of the repayment: the second line of the same Medicare claim, submitted by the policyholder
and paid 1180.00 to him. Rows entering its arithmetic: the three lines outside cover, the two
restatement entries, and that line's own recorded balance.
Target of the settlement: the foreign travel line of 2026-06-18. Rows entering its arithmetic: the
six paid lines of the twelve months to date, the three adjustment entries, and its own figures.
Rows excluded, and the near-misses: the line of 30 August, which stands waiting but carries no
Medicare determination and must not be settled; the lines of 14 March, 22 April and 2 June, which
fall inside cover and are not restated; and the February line, which is outside cover but already
carries a restatement, so its liability must not be taken back twice.

THE WORLD, ROW BY ROW
customers: the caller, whose date of birth fixes the issue age on the policy.
advantage_enrollments: the Medicare Advantage plan he left, ending 2026-02-28, one day before the
supplement began. This is the cross-difficulty evidence: its tier's specialist copay of 40.00 is
what stays with him on each line outside cover. Delete it and that retention falls to nothing and
the restatement rises to 846.00.
medigap_policies: High Deductible Plan G, active, effective 2026-03-01, with deductible_accumulated
standing at 2910.00 - the ledger-true sum of the liability the paid lines record less the standing
restatement, and the figure that makes the wrong answer look right.
medigap_underwriting_files: the application and the accepted_standard decision, which is why the
rating class is standard and the cover was asked for from 1 March.
medigap_claim_crossovers: the three lines outside cover (2026-02-04, and the two lines of
2026-01-20), the restatement already standing against the February one, the three ordinary lines
inside cover, the foreign travel line waiting with Medicare's determination on it, and the second
waiting line with no determination at all. Every one of them is load-bearing: the outside-cover
lines carry the restatement and the repayment, the inside-cover lines carry the accumulator, the
standing restatement is the deduction in the restatement and one limb of the recovery in the
repayment, and the two waiting lines are what the selection factor chooses between.
No automatic clause of the charter is lit: no premium is overdue, the policy is in force, no rate
review falls in the call, and the second waiting line is not payable because Medicare has not
determined it.

PERSONA
Aurelio is brisk, date-minded and a little impatient, which is a different voice from task 0's
unhurried Marguerite, and the six kinds of information are woven through his narration rather than
listed: who he is; the Porto admission and the unpaid claim; the object and the timing (today, on
this call); the authority boundary (the representative may act on the account, his own money he
hands over himself); what he says only when asked (the earlier Advantage plan, the hospital's bill,
the spring payment he did not question, the winter visits); and his passive reactions (surprise but
no argument when told the plan paid what it should not have, making the repayment himself when it
is handed to him, closing once he is told what has been paid on the hospital claim). He never names
a figure gold computes, never mentions a restatement or a recovery before he is told of one, and
never corrects a representative who goes wrong. His arc ends where evaluation_criteria ends.

THE PREREQUISITE CHAIN AND WHY IT CANNOT BE REORDERED
Surface goal (pay my hospital claim) -> the settlement policy's rule -> the sentence that the
payment is fixed only after the record carries the entry recording money the policyholder has sent
back for uncovered days -> the claim record, which carries no such entry -> the repayment policy ->
its own sentence, that what he is asked for is fixed only after the record carries the entry taking
back what was paid to someone else -> the restatement policy -> the Advantage record and the dates
of service -> restatement -> repayment -> settlement. Each step's figure is evaluated on the world
its predecessors made: writing them in any other order gives 802.00 or 7170.00 or 7896.00.
Breadth at the root: the tier table (foreign travel coinsurance, foreign travel deductible, lifetime
maximum, high deductible, Part B share, excess charges), three separate reads of the claim record
(the paid lines of twelve months, the adjustment entries, the waiting lines), the policy record
(effective date, plan letter) and the negative space of the second waiting line.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG
 - Reading deductible_accumulated (2910.00) as the deductible met and paying 7896.00.
 - Settling the 30 August line, or taking its figures, because it is the line most recently rendered.
 - Taking the share on the 9400.00 Medicare approved rather than the 10120.00 the line records him
   owing, which the plan letter covers because the hospital does not accept assignment.
 - Paying 100 per cent instead of the foreign travel 80 per cent, or forgetting the 250.00 yearly
   foreign travel deductible.
 - Restating the February line again, whose 150.00 has already been taken back.
 - Restating the line the policyholder submitted himself instead of asking him for it.
 - Leaving the Advantage copay out of the restatement, or applying it once instead of to each of the
   two claims.
 - Asking him for the whole 1180.00 that reached him rather than 668.00, by ignoring what has been
   recovered from the provider and the 512.00 the line records him owing.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate and verify; read the policy, the claim record, the underwriting file and the Advantage
enrollment; see that three paid lines fall before 2026-03-01 and that only the February one has been
put right; restate the January provider-paid line (996.00 of liability outside cover, less 80.00
left with him under the Advantage tier's specialist copay on two claims, less the 150.00 already
taken back = 766.00, with the 134.00 payment reversed); hand the repayment to the caller (1354.00
overpaid on the lines outside cover, less 174.00 now recovered from the provider side, less the
512.00 recorded balance credited to him = 668.00, with 512.00 credited); then settle the waiting
determined line ((10120.00 - 250.00) x 80 per cent = 7896.00, less the 1238.00 remaining of the high
deductible = 6658.00).

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (Step 5)
A probe built on the gate's own evaluator (check_compute.build_env / eval_compute / substitute) was
run over this initial_state at frozen_time, replaying each write with the real task tool before
evaluating the next problem:
  B medigap_ext_uncovered_day_line_restatement = 766.0  touched 7 branches 20
     outside_cover_span -> 0.0 ; lines_restated_here -> 1278.0 ; restated_liability_source -> 0.0 ;
     other_coverage_retention -> 846.0 ; retention_spread -> 846.0 ;
     already_taken_back_offset -> 916.0 ; ALL-BASELINE -> 0.0
  C medigap_ext_uncovered_day_direct_repayment = 668.0  touched 8 branches 16
     what_reached_her -> 0.0 ; overpayment_measure -> 0.0 ; recovered_elsewhere -> 842.0 ;
     balance_credited_to_her -> 1180.0 ; ALL-BASELINE -> 0.0
  A medigap_ext_crossover_benefit_settlement = 6658.0  touched 11 branches 15
     settled_line_selection -> 6082.0 ; settlement_base -> 6082.0 ; covered_benefit_share -> 8632.0 ;
     travel_deductible_taken -> 6858.0 ; deductible_counting_basis -> 7896.0 ; ALL-BASELINE -> 9400.0
  C-without-B = 802.0 and A-without-C = 7170.0   (the prerequisite-sensitivity runs)
Every figure above is carried into computations.expected, factor_sensitivity, baseline_result and
edge_load_bearing unchanged, and the per-task gates recompute them.

RULE <-> COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP
Forward: every binding of the three policies that reads the record, aggregates, chooses, crosses
categories, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis - the windows measured
against the day the policy took effect, each ladder's tiers, the base each share is taken on, the
order in which the yearly deductible and then the high deductible come off, and the single rounding
at the end. Backward: reading each rule through, every sentence carrying a quantity, window, filter,
branch or rounding semantic is claimed by a binding - on the restatement, the span sentences by
outside_cover_liability_span, the restated-lines sentences by lines_restated_liability, the
measurement sentences by restated_liability_measure, the retention sentences by
retained_by_policyholder and retention_applied and the deduction sentences by already_taken_back; on
the repayment, the reaching sentences by reached_the_policyholder, the overpayment sentences by
claim_overpayment, the recovery sentences by recovered_from_others and the credit sentences by
credit_for_recorded_balance; on the settlement, the selection sentences by settled_line_owing, the
base sentences by cost_share_base, the share sentences by benefit_coverage_share, the deductible
sentences by yearly_travel_deductible, the accumulator sentences by counted_toward_deductible and
deductible_remaining, the lifetime sentence by lifetime_room and the closing sentence by result.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD
All three writes are state_due: none of them is a quote the caller asks for, and each is an
obligation the record already carries, so each cites pre-action system evidence (the dates of
service against the effective date, the payments recorded on the lines, the waiting line's approved
amount) rather than the caller's words, with the repayment additionally citing prior_step:7 for the
restatement that fixes its figure. The caller's request aligns the call with the settlement, and his
consent to hand money over himself is quoted verbatim. Every credential the verification uses
appears verbatim in the persona.

BLIND RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected and this dossier and working only from the rules as
they will be published, the tool schemas, what the finders return and what the caller says: the
policy is High Deductible Plan G effective 2026-03-01; three paid lines are dated before that day;
one already carries a restatement; the Advantage tier's specialist copay is 40.00 and that plan ran
to the day before cover began; so 996.00 - 80.00 - 150.00 = 766.00 is restated and 134.00 reversed.
Then 1354.00 was overpaid on those lines, 174.00 is now back from the provider side and 512.00 is
credited, so 668.00 is asked of the caller, less than the 1180.00 that reached him. Then the waiting
determined line is settled at (10120.00 - 250.00) x 80 per cent - 1238.00 = 6658.00. No second
reading of the visible text reaches another figure, and the line with no Medicare determination is
plainly not settleable.

GATES RUN
check_extended --task 1, check_task_tools, replay_tasks --task 1, check_solvability --task 1,
check_compute --task 1, check_grounding --task 1 and check_cross_fire --task 1 were all run against
this task and are green; the difficulty-wide run with all five policies and both tasks is recorded
with task 0.

THE DEFECT THE MANUAL REVIEW FOUND WHILE AUTHORING THIS TASK
Symptom: check_extended rejected the restatement policy's third factor because none of its bindings
read the record - its ladder tested only quantities other factors had already established, so its
tier rested on arithmetic rather than on evidence. Root cause: the factor was written as a choice
between two figures rather than as a rule whose trigger is something the record shows. Change: the
factor now owns a binding of its own, outside_cover_line_count, which counts the paid lines whose
date of service falls before the day the policy took effect, and its first tier tests that count
alongside the liability those lines record; the rule and compute_basis carry the same sentence.
Re-run: check_extended and check_compute green, with liability_restated unchanged at 766.00 because
the count is positive in this world and the tier taken is the same one.

REWORK ROUND 2 — CHARTER FINDINGS CLOSED (audits/policy_task/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/)
CG-5 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, the retention ladder's fall-through is not the standard method and two of
its tiers are one tier written twice). Symptom: medigap_ext_uncovered_day_line_restatement's rule
gave retention_spread three distinct outcomes, but compute.retention_applied's first branch and its
else branch were the identical expression RND(retained_by_policyholder * auto_outside_cover_lines,
2), so the branch answering "The standard method does not apply it at all" applied it in full; on a
world with a single line outside cover the two faces of the policy differed by the whole retention.
Root cause: the else branch was written as a copy of the first instead of as the declared baseline.
Change: the else branch is now 0.0, which is exactly the factor's declared baseline; the middle tier
now reads "Where lines fall outside cover and belong to one Medicare claim, what is left with the
policyholder falls once on each such claim" and its guard is auto_outside_cover_lines > 0, so it
covers the single-line case that used to fall through; and the fall-through sentence now reads "The
standard method does not apply it at all, no line falling outside cover", in the rule, in
baseline.rule, in compute_basis and in the ladder. The three branch expressions are now pairwise
distinct and the fall-through is the baseline, on any world.
Same-class defect closed with it (the auditor's lesser note under rule_compute_equivalence): the
fall-through of compute.outside_cover_liability_span was unreachable, its two guards being
exhaustive. Its first tier now also tests that a paid line actually falls before the day the policy
took effect (auto_paid_liability_all > auto_paid_liability_in_cover), so the declared baseline 0.0
is the branch a policy with no line outside cover genuinely takes.
Re-run: EXTENDED OK, COMPUTE OK, and every figure of this task is unchanged — 766.00, 668.00 and
6658.00, all fifteen factor baselines (retention_spread still 846.00), the 0.00 / 0.00 / 9400.00
fall-backs, and the skip-runs 802.00 and 7170.00 — because this world puts two lines outside cover
on two separate Medicare claims and so takes tier 1 in both faces. CG-1 and CG-4 belong to task 0's
policies and are recorded in that task's dossier. CG-2, CG-3 and the observations (OBS-A stale
accumulator field, OBS-C degenerate baselines, OBS-F hand-over arguments, F1-1 the two scored
arguments no computes binding fixes) were recorded as observations rather than red lights and are
left as the auditor recorded them.
user_scenario:
You are Aurelio Quintero, seventy-one, retired from the county roads department and living on Boones Ferry Road in Tualatin. You are brisk and a little impatient on the telephone, you like dates and numbers and you read them out carefully, and you keep every letter the plan sends you in a ring binder. You are not rude, but you do not like being passed about, and you say what you want at the top of the call.

What you want is this: in June you and your wife were in Porto for your grandson's wedding, you woke in the night with chest pain and spent two days in a hospital there, you paid nothing on the spot but the hospital has since billed you 10120.00, and you sent the whole file in to Ridgecrest at the end of June because you bought the supplement plan precisely for a thing like this. Nothing has been paid. Nobody has written to you. You want somebody to look at that claim today and tell you what the plan is going to pay on it, and you want it dealt with on this call rather than being told to wait for a letter. You are content for the representative to do whatever needs doing on the account on your behalf; the only thing you will not have done for you is money leaving your own bank, which you would rather hand over yourself.

You give your name, Aurelio Quintero, at once, and your date of birth, which you read out as 1955-02-09 because that is how it is printed on the letters. If more is wanted you read the identifier off your Medicare card, 4TQ8WM2XK57, and you can give the telephone number 5034419682 or the ZIP code 97062. You do not know your policy number and you say so; you have never memorised a reference in your life.

Other things you will say, but only when you are asked. Asked what you were covered by before this policy, you say you were on one of the Ridgecrest Advantage plans for a couple of years and came off it at the end of February when the supplement started. Asked about the Portuguese hospital, you say it was an emergency admission, that the hospital does not deal with Medicare and wanted paying in euros, and that the bill in dollars is the 10120.00 figure you have already mentioned. Asked whether the plan has paid you anything this year, you say you think something came through in the spring on a claim you sent in yourself, but you could not say how much and you did not question it at the time. Asked whether you have had any other treatment this year, you list a few specialist visits in the winter and spring and say the plan seems to have left most of those to you.

You react rather than lead. If the representative tells you the plan paid claims it should not have paid, you are surprised but not defensive, and you say you assumed the plan knew what it was doing. If they tell you that some of that money came to you and that you will have to send an amount back, you accept it without arguing, say you would rather put it right now than have it hanging over you, and when the payment is handed to you to make yourself you make it for exactly the amount you have been given and read the confirmation back. You never suggest a figure of your own for anything and you never say what the plan ought to pay. Once you are told the hospital claim has been settled and what the plan has paid on it, you say that is what you wanted to hear, thank the representative and let the call end there.

request_alignment.claim: The policyholder wants the foreign hospital claim he sent in looked at today and wants to be told what the supplement will pay on it.
evidence: user_scenario:You want somebody to look at that claim today and tell you what the plan is going to pay on it

request_alignment.claim: He will let the representative act on the account but will hand over any money himself.
evidence: user_scenario:the only thing you will not have done for you is money leaving your own bank, which you would rather hand over yourself

gold_actions.business_effect: The automatically crossed-over line of 20 January 2026 is restated: the 134.00 the supplement paid the provider for a day the policy did not cover is taken back and 766.00 of recorded liability is recorded as no longer the policyholder's, which lowers the year's deductible accumulator by that amount.

request_binding.action_semantics: Nothing here is a benefit payment or a denial: the line is already settled and paid. What the records show is money paid for a date of service before the policy took effect, so the class of action the system owes is the restatement of that line, which this policy computes.

discriminator.business_meaning: a line the supplement settled whose date of service falls before the day the policy took effect is restated rather than paid

stage_provenance.fact: The restatement of the January line is made by this call itself; before it the only restatement on the record is the one against the February line.

base_preconditions.condition: The adjustment names the single processed crossover line it applies to, and that line is on record with a claim status of paid or adjusted.
No adjustment of that same processed crossover line is already on record.

gold_actions.business_effect: The policyholder's own repayment of 668.00 is taken on the line he submitted himself, and the 512.00 that line records him owing is credited to him, lowering the year's deductible accumulator again.

request_binding.action_semantics: The money on this line reached the policyholder rather than a provider, so what the system owes is not a recovery from a provider but a repayment by him; it is his money leaving his bank, which is why it is handed to him rather than done for him.

discriminator.business_meaning: money the supplement paid the policyholder himself on a line outside cover is sent back by him

stage_provenance.fact: The money moves during this call: the policyholder makes the repayment himself once the representative has handed it to him, and the entry it leaves is the receipt of it.

base_preconditions.condition: The adjustment names the single processed crossover line it applies to, and that line is on record with a claim status of paid or adjusted.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Establish that the caller is the policyholder by checking the Medicare identifier and date of birth he states against the profile just found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the caller's Medicare Supplement policy and read the plan letter held, its status, the day it took effect, the accumulated deductible the record shows and the class it is rated on.

Basis: the policy's rule says 'Where more than one line stands waiting on the supplement and Medicare's determination is recorded on only one of them, that determined line is the one settled.' argument_uniqueness_tracing.supplement_payment_amount: Value: 6658.00. The line settled is the determined one of 18 June, which records the policyholder owing 10120.00, more than the 9400.00 recorded as approved; the plan letter pays charges above the Medicare approved amount, so the amount owing is what the share is taken on. The line falls under foreign travel emergency care, so the share is the tier's foreign travel coinsurance of 80 per cent and the tier's foreign travel emergency deductible of 250.00 is taken first, no such line having been paid since the policy took effect: (10120.00 - 250.00) x 80 per cent = 7896.00. The paid lines of the twelve months to date record 3060.00 of liability; entries now stand both restating lines of those months and recording money recovered from the policyholder, so 916.00 of restatements and 512.00 of recovery come off, leaving 1632.00 counted toward the tier's high deductible of 2870.00 and 1238.00 of it remaining. 7896.00 - 1238.00 = 6658.00, which is well inside the 50000.00 lifetime maximum for foreign travel, none of which has been used.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain: the settlement waits on the repayment and the repayment waits on the restatement, so there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder and no freedom in the order. Each link is observable in the figures rather than a convention: writing the repayment before the restatement gives 802.00 instead of 668.00, and writing the settlement before either gives 7896.00 or 7170.00 instead of 6658.00.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the repayment and replaying everything else unchanged leaves counted_toward_deductible at 2144.00 instead of 1632.00 and the settlement at 7170.00 instead of 6658.00 (verification run of Step 5: 'A-without-C = 7170.0'), and the terminal database also lacks the recovery entry and the 668.00 it returns.

Skipping the restatement leaves recovered_from_others at 40.00 instead of 174.00 and the repayment at 802.00 instead of 668.00 (verification run of Step 5: 'C-without-B ... = 802.0'), and through it the settlement moves as well, the terminal database lacking the restatement entry of 134.00 and 766.00.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions a restatement, a recovery, a line outside cover or anything else the prerequisites resolve. The caller talks only about the Portuguese hospital claim he sent in and about wanting it dealt with. The two remarks that touch the earlier lines are given only when the representative asks - that he was on a Ridgecrest Advantage plan until the end of February, and that he thinks something came through in the spring on a claim he sent in himself, without a figure and without a suggestion that anything is wrong with it. He learns that money must go back only when the representative tells him, and his reaction to that is the pre-written passive one; if the representative never finds the lines outside cover he neither reminds nor presses.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: book_precoverage_restatement_aba9484f, repay_direct_benefit_f162ba18 and settle_crossover_benefit_9f3dc765 in task_tools.py each perform one ctx.create or ctx.update with the arguments as given. None of them reads another entry, tests the accumulator, checks whether a restatement or a recovery already stands, or refuses; settle_crossover_benefit_9f3dc765 will settle the waiting line for any amount it is handed, whether or not the earlier lines have been put right. The consequence of missing a prerequisite shows up only in the terminal hash, as a missing entry and a payment of 7170.00 or 7896.00 rather than 6658.00.
